issues.t: Head gasket leaks
issues.sym: Oil or coolant seeping from where the cylinder heads meet the engine block, a sweet coolant smell, the coolant level dropping, the temperature gauge rising, or a rough idle with misfire codes.
issues.why: The 2.5L four-cylinder of these years used head gaskets that break down with age. On the 1996-1999 engine they tend to fail inside and cause overheating; on 2000 and later engines they usually start as slow outside leaks of oil and coolant.
issues.next: Check coolant and oil levels often and watch the temperature gauge. If it starts to overheat, pull over and shut it off. Get a cooling system pressure test, and plan the repair before a small leak becomes an overheated engine.

issues.t: AWD binding in tight turns (automatic)
issues.sym: In tight, slow turns such as parking lots, the car feels like it is braking itself, the tires scrub or hop, and the steering feels heavy.
issues.why: On automatic all-wheel-drive Legacys of this era, the transfer clutch that splits power front to rear can stay locked when it should slip. A sticking transfer (duty C) solenoid, worn clutch plates, or mismatched tire sizes are the usual causes.
issues.next: First make sure all four tires are the same brand, size and wear, and that the transmission fluid is full and clean. If it still binds, have a Subaru-savvy shop test the transfer solenoid before parts wear further.

issues.t: Timing belt breaks and damages the engine
issues.sym: The engine suddenly stops while driving, then cranks but will not start. There may be no warning at all.
issues.why: These engines use a rubber timing belt, and the valves and pistons can hit each other if it breaks or skips. Belts that are past their replacement interval, or worn idler pulleys and the belt tensioner, are the usual cause.
issues.next: If your service records do not show a timing belt change on schedule, have it done now along with the idlers and tensioner. If the belt already broke, do not keep cranking the engine; have it towed and checked for bent valves.

issues.t: Automatic transmission slipping or slow to engage
issues.sym: A delay or a clunk when shifting into Drive, slipping or flaring between gears, or the car not wanting to move at all.
issues.why: Owners of these years report worn automatic transmissions, often after high mileage. Old or low fluid and internal clutch wear are common causes.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and condition. If it slips or will not engage, avoid hard driving and get a transmission diagnosis; a rebuild or used unit is often needed.

issues.t: Engine bearing failure and knocking
issues.sym: A deep knocking from the engine that gets louder with speed, low oil pressure, and sometimes the engine seizing.
issues.why: Owners of 2000 Legacys reported crankshaft and rod bearing failures at fairly low mileage. Once a bearing wears through, the engine is badly damaged.
issues.next: If you hear a new knock, stop driving and check the oil level. Keep oil changes on time. A knocking engine usually needs a replacement or rebuild.

issues.t: Turbocharger failure from oil starvation
issues.sym: Whining or siren noise from the engine, blue smoke from the exhaust, loss of boost and power, or a check engine light with codes P0011 or P0021.
issues.why: The turbo on the GT is fed oil through a bolt with a fine filter screen that can clog with sludge. Starved of oil, the turbo bearings wear out. Late or skipped oil changes make it far more likely.
issues.next: Use the correct full-synthetic oil and change it on time. If you get P0011/P0021 codes, have the oil feed screens checked right away; they are an early warning. A smoking turbo needs to be replaced before it damages the engine.

issues.t: CVT shudder, jerking or failure
issues.sym: A shudder or vibration when pulling away, jerky or hesitant acceleration, whining, stalling when coming to a stop, or a flashing AWD or transmission warning light.
issues.why: The CVT automatic used with the 2.5L engine can develop torque converter and valve body faults. Subaru extended the warranty on these CVTs to 10 years or 100,000 miles because of the number of failures.
issues.next: Ask a Subaru dealer with your VIN whether the extended coverage still applies. Have the CVT fluid checked and the computer updated; do not ignore a shudder, because it can get worse.

issues.t: Excessive oil consumption
issues.sym: The oil level drops a lot between changes, the low-oil light comes on, or you have to add a quart or more every few thousand miles.
issues.why: Early FB25 engines had piston rings that let oil slip past and burn. A class settlement extended Subaru coverage for this to 8 years or 100,000 miles.
issues.next: Check the oil level every fuel stop or two and top it up so the engine never runs low. Ask a Subaru dealer for an oil consumption test and whether any coverage remains.

issues.t: Battery drains while parked
issues.sym: The car will not start or needs a jump after sitting a day or two, sometimes over and over.
issues.why: Owners say some computer modules keep drawing power after the car is shut off, which wears down the battery. Subaru settled a class action that extended coverage for qualifying batteries; it did not admit a defect.
issues.next: Have the battery tested and check for a parasitic drain. Ask the dealer about software updates and whether settlement coverage applies to your car.

issues.t: Thermo control valve fault
issues.sym: Check engine light with codes like P26A3 or P26A5, weak cabin heat, or the engine running warm.
issues.why: An electronic valve that routes coolant on the 2.5L engine can stick or lose its position signal. Subaru extended coverage on this valve to 15 years or 150,000 miles.
issues.next: Ask a Subaru dealer with your VIN; the repair should be free under the extension. Watch the temperature gauge and stop if it climbs.

issues.t: Windshield cracks with no clear impact
issues.sym: A crack appears or spreads from the edge of the windshield, sometimes after only a tiny chip or none at all.
issues.why: Many owners report windshields cracking easily. A class settlement offers reimbursement and an extended one-time replacement with an updated windshield; Subaru denied a defect.
issues.next: Ask a dealer whether the settlement coverage applies. After any windshield replacement the EyeSight cameras must be recalibrated so driver aids work correctly.

issues.t: Touchscreen freezes, blanks or reboots
issues.sym: The center touchscreen freezes, goes black, restarts by itself, ignores touches, or drops Apple CarPlay or Android Auto.
issues.why: Software faults in the infotainment unit are behind most cases. Subaru has issued several bulletins with updates for screens that flash, stop responding or shut off.
issues.next: Ask the dealer for the latest infotainment software update. Since climate controls are in the screen on many trims, get it fixed rather than living with it.

issues.t: Passenger airbag stays off for a lighter adult
issues.sym: The PASSENGER AIRBAG ON light does not come on, or switches on and off, when a smaller adult sits in the front seat.
issues.why: The seat sensor decides whether to enable the airbag based on weight. Owners of recent Legacys filed federal complaints that it leaves the airbag off for lighter adults, and dealers said the system was working as designed.
issues.next: Watch the airbag status light every trip. If it shows OFF with an adult seated, ask the dealer to test the occupant sensor and report it to NHTSA. Children under 13 belong in the back seat.

issues.t: EyeSight brakes hard for no reason
issues.sym: The car brakes suddenly for parked cars or nothing at all, which can surprise drivers behind you.
issues.why: Owners filed federal complaints about the forward collision braking reacting to things that are not a threat.
issues.next: Keep the windshield clean in front of the cameras and report each event to the dealer so they can check for software updates and camera alignment.

issues.t: Windshield chips and cracks from small stones
issues.sym: Small stones at highway speed chip or crack the windshield, sometimes more than once on a low-mileage car.
issues.why: Owners report windshields that crack easily from road debris, similar to complaints on earlier Legacys.
issues.next: Repair chips quickly before they spread. If the windshield is replaced, the EyeSight cameras must be recalibrated.

issues.t: Engine stalls on the highway and will not restart right away
issues.sym: The engine shuts off while driving and will not restart for several minutes.
issues.why: A few owners have filed federal complaints describing this; dealers had not found a cause in those reports.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. If it happens, put the hazards on and steer to the shoulder. Report it to the dealer right away with the date and conditions so codes can be read while fresh.

issues.t: Exhaust smell in the cabin or smoke from the tailpipe
issues.sym: Engine or exhaust fumes in the cabin, or white smoke from the exhaust with a rough running engine.
issues.why: Owners have filed federal complaints describing an exhaust leak at the manifold and white smoke with a misfire that returned after dealer repairs.
issues.next: Exhaust fumes in the cabin can be dangerous. Drive with fresh air on and windows cracked, and get it checked under warranty promptly.

issues.t: Takata passenger airbag inflator (recall)
issues.sym: There is usually no warning. The danger only shows up in a crash, when the passenger airbag deploys.
issues.why: The Takata inflator can break down after years of heat and humidity and burst when the airbag fires, throwing metal pieces into the cabin. Some earlier replacement inflators were also recalled.
issues.next: Check your VIN on NHTSA or Subaru's site today. If the recall is open, contact a Subaru dealer right away; the repair is free.

issues.t: Brake lines can rust through (recall)
issues.sym: A soft or sinking brake pedal, brake fluid under the car, or the brake warning light.
issues.why: In salt-belt states, salty water can splash past the fuel tank guard and rust the brake lines until they leak, which makes the car take longer to stop.
issues.next: If the brake pedal suddenly turns hard or a red brake warning comes on, press the pedal much harder than normal, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — call for a tow. If the pedal feels soft, get the car checked before driving it more. Check your VIN; dealers inspect, coat and replace leaking lines for free.

issues.t: Secondary air pump relay can stick on (recall)
issues.sym: A whirring pump that keeps running and a burning plastic smell from the engine bay.
issues.why: The relay for the emissions air pump can fail closed, so the pump runs all the time, overheats and can melt, which is a fire risk.
issues.next: If you smell burning plastic, shut the car off and park it outside. Check your VIN; dealers replace the relay for free.

issues.t: Ignition switch can shut the engine off (recall)
issues.sym: The engine can switch off while driving, with loss of power steering and brake assist.
issues.why: A spring inside the ignition switch can break, letting the switch move out of the run position.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Check your VIN. Keep heavy key rings off the key until it is fixed. The dealer repair is free.

issues.t: Wiper motor cover can overheat and melt (recall)
issues.sym: The wipers stop working in snow or ice, and you may smell something burning near the base of the windshield.
issues.why: Debris inside the wiper motor can make it bind. If the wipers cannot reach their parked spot, the motor overheats and its cover can melt, which could cause a fire.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and call 911 if there are flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. Clear snow and ice off the wipers before switching them on. Check your VIN; the dealer replaces the part free.

issues.t: Electronic parking brake may not hold (manual transmission, recall)
issues.sym: On manual-transmission cars, the parking brake may not keep the car still on a slope.
issues.why: The electronic parking brake on manual cars may not apply enough force, so the car can roll away.
issues.next: Leave the car in gear and turn the wheels toward the curb when parked on a hill. Check your VIN for the free repair.

issues.t: Transmission oil can leak onto exhaust (recall)
issues.sym: Smoke or a hot oil smell from under the car, or spots of oil under it.
issues.why: A bent seal cap can let transmission oil leak onto the hot exhaust, which can start a fire.
issues.next: If you see smoke, pull over and turn the car off. Check your VIN for the free repair. NHTSA recall number: 15V-502.

issues.t: Steering column may be machined wrong (do-not-drive recall)
issues.sym: Steering feels loose, or turning the wheel may not steer the car.
issues.why: Some steering columns built in spring 2016 may have been machined wrong. NHTSA listed this as do-not-drive until repaired.
issues.next: Check your VIN right away. If it is affected, do not drive it; ask the dealer to tow it in for the free repair. NHTSA recall number: 16V-292.

issues.t: Knee airbag bracket may not be attached (recall)
issues.sym: No symptoms. It only matters in a crash.
issues.why: A bracket that supports the driver knee guard may not be fastened properly to the steering support beam, so it may not protect the driver as designed.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the free inspection and repair.

issues.t: Low-pressure fuel pump may fail (recall)
issues.sym: Rough running, the check engine light, stalling while driving, or the engine not starting.
issues.why: The low-pressure fuel pump in the tank can stop working, which can stall the engine without warning.
issues.next: Check your VIN. If the engine stalls, get to a safe spot and have it towed. Dealers replace the pump free. NHTSA recall number: 21V-587.

issues.t: Low-fuel warning may read wrong (recall)
issues.sym: The fuel gauge shows more range than you really have, and the low-fuel light may not come on in time.
issues.why: A software error can make the low-fuel warning and miles-to-empty display wrong, so you could run out of fuel.
issues.next: Fill up early until the free software fix is done. Check your VIN.

issues.t: Body spot welds may be missing (recall)
issues.sym: No symptoms. It only matters in a crash.
issues.why: Some cars were built with spot welds missing or done poorly, which weakens the body in a crash.
issues.next: Check your VIN; Subaru inspects affected cars and fixes or replaces them.

issues.t: CVT drive chain can slip and break (recall)
issues.sym: Sudden loss of drive power and a transmission warning light.
issues.why: A programming error in the CVT computer can let a clutch engage before the drive chain is clamped, so the chain can slip and break.
issues.next: Check your VIN. Dealers update the software and replace the CVT if the chain already slipped. NHTSA recall numbers: 21V-955, 22V-485.

issues.t: Passenger occupant sensor may shut off airbag (recall)
issues.sym: The passenger airbag OFF light stays on even with an adult in the seat.
issues.why: A part in the passenger seat occupant sensor can crack and short, which can turn off the passenger airbag.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the free sensor replacement. Until then, the passenger airbag may not deploy. NHTSA recall number: 24V-227.

issues.t: Water in inhibitor switch disables reverse lights and camera (recall)
issues.sym: The reverse lights or backup camera may stop working, and the transmission warning light may come on.
issues.why: Water can get into the transmission range (inhibitor) switch through a weak weld and make it fail.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the free switch replacement. Back up carefully if the camera is out.

issues.t: Driveshaft center support bolts can loosen (recall)
issues.sym: A clunk or vibration from under the middle of the car.
issues.why: Bolts holding the driveshaft center support can work loose, letting the front end of the driveshaft come off.
issues.next: Check your VIN; dealers fit new bolts free.

issues.t: Front coil springs can rust and break (recall)
issues.sym: A loud bang or clunk from the front, the car sitting low on one corner, or a tire being cut by a broken spring.
issues.why: Front coil springs with poor paint can rust in salt areas and break, and a broken piece can puncture the tire.
issues.next: Check your VIN. A broken spring is unsafe; have it towed in.

issues.t: Rear subframe can rust and break (recall)
issues.sym: Clunks from the rear, odd handling, or visible heavy rust under the back of the car.
issues.why: Rear subframes with poor paint can rust through in salt areas and break.
issues.next: Check your VIN and have the rear subframe inspected.
